scenario: I am a wildlife photographer, not a programmer, and want a project that sorts new wildlife photos into suggested social-media carousel packs. When I add a batch, group related sightings, make useful carousel copies, suggest captions or metadata, and add a map card only when location is safe. I want suggestions on my phone and approve before sharing. Keep originals untouched forever. Blurry photos, duplicates, missing locations, and photos that do not fit should be called out, not discarded. Phone delivery could use cloud album, messages, or another service. Square versus portrait, carousel size, and exact-coordinate policy are undecided. I know folders contain JPEG and HEIC and I can review weekly. I do not want to manually prepare every image. Fixtures are synthetic. Produce a clear brief preserving automatic flow, stating questions I must answer, and do not claim processing or delivery occurred.

attachments.sample-wildlife-folder.txt: SYNTHETIC: fox-01.jpg, heron-02.heic, fox-01-copy.jpg; duplicate and missing location.

APPLY IT TO YOUR PROJECT
Describe your task. Let your AI consult the guide.

Use your own model to choose an approach that delivers your outcome and the amount of work you want to hand over. Give it a brief, or ask it to fetch the reference directly. You do not need to choose a level first.

Make your project brief

A rough description is enough. Your model will ask about important gaps.

Start with your own words or try an example. Examples fill empty answers only, so your edits stay intact. Nothing is sent to a model here; copy or download before leaving.

Photography example
Weekly report example
Engineering example

1. What do you want done?

Example: “Turn an outing’s wildlife photos into ready-to-post carousels on my phone.”

2. What should you still do yourself?

Choose a starting point, edit it, or leave this blank if you are unsure.

Review finished results.
Approve important actions.
Work alongside the AI.
Help me decide.
3. Anything it should know or never do?

Example: “My photos are on a Windows PC. I use an iPhone. Never delete originals.”

Add context or example files (optional)
Your brief to copy or download

The preview updates as you type. Your model will make the recommendation in your own conversation.

Copy brief
Download Markdown

1. Describe the work

Describe what starts the process, what should be ready at the end, and what you want to do yourself. Leave unknowns blank so your model can ask.

2. Hand it to your model

Copy or download your brief and attach relevant workflow files in your own agent. Your model should ask a few short, numbered questions, with one main decision each, then provide a concise recommendation. If your model can browse, it can fetch the guide and relevant concept pages itself.

3. Review the recommendation

Check every recurring manual step against the experience you asked for. The initial plan should be concise, distinguish confirmed requirements from untested assumptions, and explain alternatives and checks. Ask for deeper implementation detail when you need it.

Levels describe autonomy, not a ranking of solutions. Prefer simplicity among approaches that meet your needs—not by giving unwanted work back to you. A fixed workflow can be fully automated; an agent can be worthwhile when it removes substantial hands-on effort.

Build tools, then use them

For tasks that need custom processing or connections between systems, ask your model to consider a coding agent that builds or adapts a tool, tests it, runs it, and inspects the result. For example, it might create a project-data collector and a report generator, then use them to prepare a weekly report for review. The resulting tools may later run as ordinary software; you do not necessarily need an agent in every recurring run. Compare reuse, development effort, validation, and execution permissions before choosing.

Explore coding agents → · See how a harness bounds their work →

Ready to go further?

Once your approach is clear, create agent instructions, describe the workflow, or define how to check success. Use only the tools that help your project.

Browse all project tools →
Agent instructions
Workflow designer
Definition of done
Bring examples of your current workflow

Send your brief and relevant files to your own agent together. Text, Markdown, photos, spreadsheets, reports, and other files can show details that are hard to describe.

Current input: a representative file the process starts with.
Current output: what you produce today, with what you like and what should improve.
Desired output: a finished example or annotated mockup, if you have one.
Exceptions and instructions: an awkward case, a failed result, or a format the system must follow.

In the brief, name each file and its role. Attach those files separately in your agent, or give a local agent explicit access to the relevant folder. The brief download contains text only; this website does not upload or package your files. If a format is unsupported, provide an export or preview your model can inspect.

Let your model fetch the reference

Give your model your task and this address: https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/agents.md. The guide links to the index, concept definitions, relationships, worked examples, and sources. Models with browsing or retrieval tools can follow those links; fetching is not automatic in every chat app.

If your model cannot browse, attach the relevant concept Markdown pages or the reference text along with your brief. The full export is large; individual pages may fit better. Ask the model to state what it actually read.
